candidates.counter_evidence_explanation: Gateway, inventory and payment metrics are healthy (p95 72ms, low error rate), so the leak is not yet shown to cause the checkout degradation.
missing_evidence: Order p95 latency and error rate trend over a longer window to link retention to checkout degradation
Heap profile or allocation-site data identifying the leaking structure in order
candidates.statement: Order service shows sustained heap retention: retained_bytes rises 49.3MB to 81.3MB across 5 samples with net allocations 8000, retained_after_gc true, and 7 retained_heap_after_gc WARN logs, consistent with a memory leak in order.
candidates.uncertainty: Retention is below the 160MB limit and order p95 is 72ms; causal link to checkout health is not established.

report.explanation: Order is the only service with anomalous memory retention (sustained growth, retained after GC, WARN logs), while gateway, inventory and payment are healthy. A bounded memory-leak candidate in order is supported, but the link to checkout degradation remains unproven.
